findings.title: Creating codes in user storage leaves any prior local recovery credential active
findings.body: When a user storage provider starts accepting recovery-code updates, this path returns after `updateCredential` succeeds and does not remove an existing local `recovery-authn-codes` credential. This can occur for users whose codes were previously created locally because the provider did not support the type, or after a provider configuration/upgrade change. The local credential provider replaces its own credential during regeneration, but here the old local codes remain. Credential validation can still fall back to that local credential when the new user-storage credential rejects an old code, so previously issued recovery codes can remain valid after the user regenerates them. On successful user-storage creation, the implementation needs to invalidate/remove any local credential of this type (or otherwise ensure validation cannot use it).
